Answer: B
Reason: The HRCT images (Figures 2a and 2d) demonstrate a combination of nodules and cysts with a distinct upper-to-mid lung zone predominance and sparing of the costophrenic angles, which is the classic radiological hallmark of Pulmonary Langerhans' Cell Histiocytosis (PLCH). Although PLCH typically spares the pleura, the specific distribution of the parenchymal findings (upper lobe nodules/cysts) strongly points to this diagnosis over lower-zone predominant diseases like heart failure or idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
